transcript: you can see Broadway legend Andre De Shields do push-ups in a site specific production of a classic play but you might not be the same afterward last week I was invited to this revival of Moliere's comedy Tartuffe Performed in this centuries-old library that was literally shipped from Italy to New York by the Vanderbilts with an ornate mansion built around it normally it isn't even open for public viewing as it's used by the Episcopal Church and this is actually the first theatrical production to be staged here which is kind of hard to believe because this space is so perfect for seeing theatre the style of comedy in this version of Tartuffe is very playful and campy there’s self aware humor audience interaction bits thrown in there but also baked into the play is a bit of a satirical edge that slightly (or not so lightly) echoes some elements of modern society not to mention this is a very exciting cast that is clearly having a ton of fun up there on stage and of course they're led by the truly inimitable Tony winning Andre De Shields whose performance is everything you'd expect it to be so you can catch him as Tartuffe at New York's House of the Redeemer on the Upper East Side through November 23rd and if you get a VIP ticket you can also do this little scavenger hunt before the show which was super charming
classificationReason: Creator attended ('last week I was invited') and shares first-hand opinions ('everything you'd expect', describes the style and cast experience) of a site-specific Molière revival starring Andre De Shields at House of the Redeemer. This production is not on the provided list.
